A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SceneSmith. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, figures, and prompt lists can be matched despite renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original scene-generation experiments, a 205-participant user study, ablations, physics evaluations, and robot-policy results across 100 generated scenes.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds GPT-5.2 baseline reruns, robot simulation demonstrations, and observed failure cases.

M1.justification: The hierarchical designer–critic–orchestrator pipeline, asset acquisition, placement tools, and physical post-processing are unchanged. Method Appendices A–J match after cross-reference normalization; the new demonstrations and limitations do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Section 4.4 adds teleoperated RB-Y1 cabinet opening and bottle placement, extending demonstrated interaction coverage to articulated manipulation. The original 210-prompt corpus and four-task, 100-scene policy evaluation remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 Table 15 adds evaluated HSM-GPT-5.2 and Holodeck-GPT-5.2 comparison variants alongside their original configurations. The existing baseline families and ablations remain. ProcTHOR appears only in the new capability matrix, not as an added empirical baseline.

E3.justification: The new model-swap control reruns HSM and Holodeck on the existing 179 room prompts using GPT-5.2 at high reasoning effort with prompts and tools fixed. Section 4.4 also introduces teleoperation and zero-shot rollouts using the LBM Eval setup. Existing evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands supplementary analysis through a base-model sensitivity control, robot-interaction case studies, and a review of 210 generated scenes illustrating six failure cases. These investigate model-related confounding, practical simulation use, and failure mechanisms beyond the retained six ablations.

E5.justification: Wilson intervals, binomial tests, FDR correction, effect sizes, and scene-level t-distribution confidence intervals are retained. Table 15 uses the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no new seed or repeated-run reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: All original numerical tables retain their values. New Table 15 reports collision/stability percentages of 31.8/36.7 for HSM-GPT-5.2 and 10.8/27.4 for Holodeck-GPT-5.2. Robot demonstrations and failure examples add qualitative findings. These are additional results, not improved same-setting SceneSmith scores.

T1.justification: The scene representation, inertia calculation, layout scoring, geometric reasoning, and non-penetration optimization are unchanged. V2 adds no mathematical definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, four stated contributions, and central claims about dense, simulation-ready scene generation retain their meaning and scope. The introduction and conclusion cite the new robot demonstrations as further support for the existing simulation-readiness claim.

C2.justification: Appendix S adds substantive explanations of retrieval errors, material limitations, spatial-reasoning failures, and constraints imposed by sequential construction. It explicitly qualifies physical-parameter accuracy, articulated-object coverage, unsupported phenomena, and untested sim-to-real transfer. Appendix O also interprets model and asset-library controls and clarifies throughput versus single-scene latency.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new control configurations and robot-demo setup, states that evaluation scenes were not discarded or regenerated, and explicitly associates cost statistics with 179 rooms. The 25-scene concurrency and eight L40S GPUs were already disclosed in Appendix A.5; their repetition does not establish changed hardware.

R1.justification: V2 adds a feature comparison with prior systems in Appendix K and citations to 3D-Generalist, LBM Eval, Lin et al.'s policy work, and TRELLIS.2. These extend research positioning and contextualize demonstrations and limitations without redefining the central novelty.

P1.justification: V2 separates scene-generation results, robot-policy evaluation, and robot demonstrations into subsections, adds comparison and limitations appendices, and reorganizes automated-evaluation subsections. Most existing prose is retained; extensive appendix renumbering does not represent extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds robot-trajectory Figure 5, failure-case Figure 34, capability Table 10, and model-control Table 15. Existing figures and numerical table structures are retained, with limited caption edits and layout shifts accommodating the additions.

improvement.justification: The model-swap control strengthens attribution of the reported advantages, while Appendix S makes failure mechanisms and applicability limits substantially clearer. The new robot demonstrations provide additional practical evidence, but remain qualitative and do not establish broad policy reliability or sim-to-real transfer. These are useful, bounded improvements to an otherwise largely unchanged method and empirical foundation.
